t: Each System Knows the Whole Program
title: Each System Knows the Whole Program
description: The whole-program data model is the notes' distinctive claim: instead of each subsystem holding its slice, every system receives the entire program as data. Updates propagate by broadcast; no subsystem is ever out of sync by design.
content:
The whole-program data model is the notes' distinctive claim: instead of each subsystem holding its slice, every system receives the entire program as data. Updates propagate by broadcast; no subsystem is ever out of sync by design.

As specified, this is a real architecture choice with real costs: broadcast-everything simplifies consistency and spends bandwidth. The record files the tradeoff honestly, which is the fix the concept needed.

The demo simulates update propagation under the broadcast model versus the slice model, counting messages each way.
